## How to use this list

The **lecture slides and lab notebooks are the main reading** for this course —
everything you are examined on is in them. The items below are *optional*
supplementary reading: textbook chapters and published articles for the days you
want to go deeper. **Nothing here is required.**

Each day lists **textbook chapters** (with the chapter title, so you can find
them in any edition) and **articles** (the original papers and applied
social-science work). Pick the textbook that suits you — you do not need all of
them. A free, runnable video/tutorial companion for each day is collected in the
[appendix](#free-online-companions) and is *not* part of this reading list.

### If you want a single book to follow

We don't teach from a textbook, but if you want one spine alongside the slides:

- **Concepts (free):** Prince, *Understanding Deep Learning* — the closest match
  to this course, and the only one covering our whole arc (incl. variational
  autoencoders, diffusion, and ethics).
- **Code (the recommended text):** Raff, *Inside Deep Learning* — PyTorch-first,
  light on maths.
- **Runnable chapters:** Zhang et al., *Dive into Deep Learning* — every chapter
  is executable PyTorch; closest to the labs.

### The books referenced below

| Short name | Full reference | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **Raff** | Raff, E. (2022). *Inside Deep Learning: Math, Algorithms, Models.* Manning. | Recommended text |
| **Burkov** | Burkov, A. (2020). *Machine Learning Engineering.* True Positive Inc. | Recommended text · <http://www.mlebook.com/> |
| **Prince** | Prince, S. J. D. (2023). *Understanding Deep Learning.* MIT Press. | Free PDF · <https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/> |
| **d2l** | Zhang, A., Lipton, Z. C., Li, M., & Smola, A. J. (2023). *Dive into Deep Learning.* Cambridge University Press. | Free · <https://d2l.ai/> |
| **Goodfellow** | Goodfellow, I., Bengio, Y., & Courville, A. (2016). *Deep Learning.* MIT Press. | Free · <https://www.deeplearningbook.org/> |
| **Nielsen** | Nielsen, M. (2015). *Neural Networks and Deep Learning.* Determination Press. | Free · <http://neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com/> |

> **Note on the recommended texts.** *Raff* is the best day-to-day companion but
> does **not** cover variational autoencoders, diffusion, or word embeddings
> (Days 7–8) — use *Prince* there. *Burkov* is an ML-engineering / lifecycle
> book; it fits Day 5 (training and evaluation discipline) and Day 12
> (deployment, monitoring), not the architecture days.

# Week 1 — Foundations

## Day 1 · What do we mean by "AI"? {#day-1}

*Mon 03 Aug*

**Textbook chapters**

- Goodfellow, Ch. 1, "Introduction."
- Prince, Ch. 1, "Introduction."
- Raff, Ch. 1, "The mechanics of learning" (§1.1).

**Articles & books**

- LeCun, Y., Bengio, Y., & Hinton, G. (2015). Deep learning. *Nature*, 521(7553), 436–444.
- Mitchell, M. (2019). *Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans.* Farrar, Straus and Giroux. (Introductory chapters.)

## Day 2 · Deep models — a primer {#day-2}

*Tue 04 Aug — perceptron → MLP, the forward pass, why non-linearity matters*

**Textbook chapters**

- Raff, Ch. 2, "Fully connected networks."
- Prince, Ch. 3, "Shallow neural networks," and Ch. 4, "Deep neural networks."
- d2l, Ch. 5, "Multilayer Perceptrons."
- Goodfellow, Ch. 6, "Deep Feedforward Networks."
- Nielsen, Ch. 1, "Using neural networks to recognize handwritten digits," and Ch. 4, "A visual proof that neural nets can compute any function."

## Day 3 · Computational graphs & the maths of AI {#day-3}

*Wed 05 Aug — linear algebra, differentiation, the chain rule, graphs*

**Textbook chapters**

- d2l, Ch. 2, "Preliminaries" (linear algebra, calculus, automatic differentiation).
- Goodfellow, Ch. 2, "Linear Algebra," and Ch. 4, "Numerical Computation."
- Raff, Ch. 1, "The mechanics of learning."

## Day 4 · Backpropagation {#day-4}

*Thu 06 Aug — loss, gradients, the backward pass, gradient descent, Adam*

**Textbook chapters**

- Nielsen, Ch. 2, "How the backpropagation algorithm works."
- Prince, Ch. 5, "Loss functions"; Ch. 6, "Fitting models"; Ch. 7, "Gradients and initialization."
- Goodfellow, Ch. 6, "Deep Feedforward Networks" (§6.5, back-propagation), and Ch. 8, "Optimization for Training Deep Models."
- Raff, Ch. 1, "The mechanics of learning."

**Articles**

- Rumelhart, D. E., Hinton, G. E., & Williams, R. J. (1986). Learning representations by back-propagating errors. *Nature*, 323(6088), 533–536.
- Kingma, D. P., & Ba, J. (2015). Adam: A method for stochastic optimization. *International Conference on Learning Representations* (arXiv:1412.6980).

## Day 5 · Feed-forward networks in PyTorch {#day-5}

*Mon 10 Aug — tensors, the training loop, activations, dropout, batch-norm, overfitting*

**Textbook chapters**

- Raff, Ch. 5, "Modern training techniques" (optimisers, normalisation, learning rate); Ch. 2, "Fully connected networks."
- Burkov, Ch. 5, "Supervised Model Training (Part 1)"; Ch. 6, "Supervised Model Training (Part 2)"; Ch. 7, "Model Evaluation."
- Prince, Ch. 8, "Measuring performance"; Ch. 9, "Regularization"; Ch. 11, "Residual networks" (batch normalisation).
- Goodfellow, Ch. 7, "Regularization for Deep Learning"; Ch. 8, "Optimization for Training Deep Models"; Ch. 11, "Practical Methodology."
- Nielsen, Ch. 3, "Improving the way neural networks learn."

**Articles**

- Hegre, H., et al. (2022). *Forecasting Fatalities.* (Working paper / VIEWS project report.) — the worked civil-war forecasting example.
- Ioffe, S., & Szegedy, C. (2015). Batch normalization: Accelerating deep network training by reducing internal covariate shift. *International Conference on Machine Learning*, 448–456.

*Tue 11 Aug — images as tensors, convolution, kernels, pooling, AlexNet*

**Textbook chapters**

- Prince, Ch. 10, "Convolutional networks."

**Articles**

- Torres, M., & Cantú, F. (2022). Learning to see: Convolutional neural networks for the analysis of social science data. *Political Analysis*, 30(1), 113–131.

- Goodfellow, Ch. 14, "Autoencoders."

**Articles**

- Kingma, D. P., & Welling, M. (2014). Auto-encoding variational Bayes. *International Conference on Learning Representations* (arXiv:1312.6114).

- Goodfellow, I., et al. (2014). Generative adversarial nets. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems*, 27.
- Lall, R., & Robinson, T. (2022). The MIDAS touch: Accurate and scalable missing-data imputation with deep learning. *Political Analysis*, 30(2), 179–196.
- Lall, R., & Robinson, T. (2023). Efficient multiple imputation for diverse data in Python and R: MIDASpy and rMIDAS. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 107, 1–38.
